subject: Renewal negotiation — term counterproposal & bench validation
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pat Lee <pat.lee@servicetools.io>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + inbound bakeoff

Hi Vanessa,

Quick note — renewal for Acme Labs is coming up in June and a couple of execs flagged that a competitor (NimbusAI) has proposed a proof-of-concept and pricing that would make them a viable replacement. They claim better token economics for our high-throughput pipelines.

Before anyone jumps, can your team run a bakeoff / benchmark against our typical production workload (60–80k real requests/day, 8k token median, heavy KV-cache usage)? We need data on p95 latency, per-token cost, and also a clear commercial counter if Redwood is competitive.

Pat from our infra team is looped for technical alignment. We want to see:
- a short mutual action plan for the bakeoff
- any term or capacity options you can offer to keep us on Redwood (discounts, dedicated pool, SLA tweaks)

Can you share availability next week for a quick 30-min sync?

Thanks,
Jordan

[Acme Labs | Platform Lead]
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Pat Lee <pat.lee@servicetools.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + inbound bakeoff

Jordan — thanks for flagging and for the context. We take displacements seriously. High-level plan below, and we can refine during the sync.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) 30-min kickoff next Tue (3/23) to agree goals + sample dataset (we'll mask anything sensitive).
2) Redwood runs a 72-hour benchmark with identical request stream + latency targets; we capture p50/p95/p99 and cost-run.
3) Joint review + side-by-side report; if results are within the agreed thresholds we will present a counterproposal for renewal terms within 48hrs.

Commercial levers we can offer if the bakeoff is conclusive:
- 12-month term with a dedicated pool (reserved capacity) to guarantee throughput.
- One-time onboarding credit to cover migration and test tooling.
- Up to 15% price concession for a committed throughput band (can increase with longer term).

I attached a short MAP that covers roles, timelines and measurable success criteria.

Available Tue 3/23: 10:00–11:00 PT or 15:00–16:00 PT — what works for you?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Acme-MAP-v1.pdf (pdf)]
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal window + inbound bakeoff — internal alignment

Team — forwarding Jordan's note. Quick asks before the kickoff:
- Marissa: CS playbook for displacement / churn prevention; we should propose an SLA addendum and dedicated CSM engagement during the bakeoff.
- Nikhil: can you draft a minimal benchmark harness and confirm what telemetry we need to collect to make the report defensible?
- Rishi/Priyom: can finance prep the tightest commercial range we can offer today (best-case / stretch) and approvals needed for an on-the-spot concession?

Goal: go into kickoff with a concrete test plan, an initial commercial stance, and a named tech lead to run the bakeoff.

Thanks — V

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal window + inbound bakeoff — benchmark checklist + harness

Putting together the benchmark checklist — draft below. I'll own running the test with Acme and Pat.

Benchmark checklist (draft):
- Test harness: replay production traffic (anonymized) for 72 hours; sample size = 100k requests/day.
- Model variants: run their primary model vs our recommended quantized variant + dedicated pool config.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, mean tokens-per-response, per-token billable cost, KV cache hit-rate, error rate, tail latency under burst.
- Environment parity: same request concurrency and warm cache conditions.
- Cost calc: capture total GPU-hours and token counts; normalize to Acme's billable token definition.
- Artifacts: raw traces, latency histograms, cost model spreadsheet, and an executive summary.

Attachments: loadtest-script.sh (small harness), S3 link with starter config. I'll need cluster creds and a window to warm the cache.

If the bakeoff shows parity on latency and <10% delta on cost, recommended commercial response: 10% concession + 6 months dedicated pool + onboarding credit. If parity is worse, escalate to Rishi for an expanded commercial package.

—Nikhil

[Attachment: loadtest-script.sh (bash)]
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmelabs.com>

Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + inbound bakeoff

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround on the plan. A couple of clarifications from our side before kickoff:
- We need a formal SLA for p95 latency for the dedicated pool (our security team requires a written target).
- The competing offer is ~20% cheaper but doesn't include a dedicated pool or guaranteed SLOs — they offered early-bird credits instead.

If Redwood can deliver a written SLO and match within ~10–12% on effective unit economics, we'll prioritize you for the renewal. Also, can you provide a one-page SOW and a DocuSign-ready quote after the bakeoff?

Available for kickoff 3/23 at 10:00 PT.

Jordan

Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Counterproposal & next steps (post-bakeoff kickoff)

Jordan — great kickoff today and thanks for the candid context. We agree: data from the bakeoff will dictate the final commercial. To move this forward, we are ready to commit the following as our initial counterproposal contingent on the bakeoff results and standard diligence: 

Redwood counterproposal (summary):
- Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for Acme Labs for 6 months, sized for 300k tokens/day peak.
- Price concession: 10% off current list for the committed throughput band (with step-up discounts if you extend to 12 months).
- Written operational SLA: p95 inference latency <350ms for the dedicated pool (measured under warm-cache conditions) and 99.9% uptime for the serving tier.
- Onboarding credit: one-time credit to offset migration and benchmark labor.
- If bakeoff shows parity on latency and <=10% delta on effective unit cost, we commit to a follow-up 12-month offer (additional price improvement and a named enterprise CSM).

Next steps / deliverables:
1) I will send a DocuSign-ready counterproposal (attached) and a one-page SOW for signature.
2) Nikhil will start the benchmark harness tomorrow; we will hand over cluster creds and sample traces to Pat.
3) Joint review meeting scheduled 72 hours after the benchmark completes.

Docs attached: Redwood-Counterproposal-AcmeLabs-20260328.pdf
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abcde-12345

If this sounds aligned, Jordan, please sign the SOW and we’ll begin the bakeoff immediately. We want to make staying with Redwood the pragmatic choice.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
